$comment: Editorial selection profiles for every designer card. catalog.json merges these records during generation. Priority means selection priority, not visual z-order.

priorityScale.preferred: Use without asking when the stated editorial trigger is present.
priorityScale.situational: Use only when it materially clarifies the spoken content.
priorityScale.explicit-only: Use only after Artur explicitly requests or approves source interruption.
priorityScale.review-needed: Designer intent is known, but Artur has not approved the operating rule yet.
priorityScale.unavailable: Do not use: dropped, archived, deferred, or not implemented.

01.useWhen: Artur explicitly asks for the channel intro animation.
01.avoidWhen: Ordinary YouTube videos; never add it by default.

02·A.avoidWhen: All productions; this pre-Mono design was dropped.

02·B.avoidWhen: Do not suggest an episode-topic card; Artur does not expect to use it.

02·C.useWhen: Artur directly requests a full-frame thesis or quote.
02·C.avoidWhen: Useful footage is visible or an overlay can carry the thought.

02·D.useWhen: Artur explicitly approves a full-frame section title.
02·D.avoidWhen: A chapter marker or spoken transition is enough.

03.useWhen: A person, role, or speaker genuinely needs identification.
03.avoidWhen: The identity is already obvious or the plate adds no information.

04.useWhen: Artur selects a caption variant for this video.

05.useWhen: The viewer must locate one exact control, region, or value.
05.avoidWhen: The callout would cover the target or merely decorate the frame.

06·A.useWhen: Two alternatives require a structured visual comparison.
06·A.avoidWhen: The source itself already shows the comparison clearly.

06·B.useWhen: A compact set of values or categories is easier to understand as a graphic.
06·B.avoidWhen: Numbers are not central to the spoken point.

07·A.useWhen: A real chapter boundary needs an approved labelled transition.
07·A.avoidWhen: Inside a continuous explanation or without transition approval.

07·B.useWhen: A real chapter boundary needs an approved visual transition without text.
07·B.avoidWhen: Inside a continuous explanation or without transition approval.

07·C.avoidWhen: All productions; this pre-Mono design was dropped.

07·D.avoidWhen: All productions; this pre-Mono design was dropped.

08.useWhen: Use only after the channel-wide watermark policy is confirmed.
08.avoidWhen: Do not infer that every video requires a persistent logo.

09.avoidWhen: All current productions until dogfood validates it.

10.useWhen: Artur approves this ending for the specific video.
10.avoidWhen: A natural source ending is stronger or no end screen was requested.

10·B.useWhen: The video genuinely continues in a named next episode and Artur approves it.
10·B.avoidWhen: Generic endings or a series promise that does not exist.

11.avoidWhen: All productions; this pre-Mono design was dropped.

12·A.useWhen: A list must temporarily become the sole visual and Artur approves hiding the source.
12·A.avoidWhen: A side-panel agenda or in-frame enumeration can preserve useful footage.

12·B.avoidWhen: All productions; this pre-Mono design was dropped.

12·C.avoidWhen: All productions; this pre-Mono design was dropped.

13·A.useWhen: The narration explicitly invites viewers to the Telegram channel and the QR earns full-frame focus.
13·A.avoidWhen: No spoken Telegram CTA or useful footage must remain visible.

13·B.useWhen: The script contains a deliberate subscription CTA and the interruption is approved.

14.avoidWhen: All video timelines; the live channel banner is managed separately.

15.useWhen: A technical term needs a concise definition that narration alone will not make memorable.
15.avoidWhen: The term is familiar or the definition would merely repeat speech.

16.useWhen: Relationships between agents or system parts need a diagram.
16.avoidWhen: A real UI demonstration already proves the relationship.

17.useWhen: A short prompt fragment must be read while the source remains visible.
17.avoidWhen: Long prompt text or duplicate captions.

18.useWhen: Comparable measured values are central to the argument.
18.avoidWhen: The numbers are anecdotal, incomparable, or incidental.

19.useWhen: The narration enumerates concrete process steps and a full-screen interruption is approved.
19.avoidWhen: Hook agenda; useful source footage is present; or the list is decorative.

20.useWhen: A factual claim relies on an external article, paper, or named source.
20.avoidWhen: No source is being cited or the citation is unverifiable.

21.useWhen: A completed action or system status needs a brief confirmation.
21.avoidWhen: The underlying UI already shows the same status clearly.

23.avoidWhen: Only one or two values are compared.

24.useWhen: A real before/after contrast is part of the evidence.
24.avoidWhen: The two states are not directly comparable.

25.avoidWhen: Minor topic shifts inside one chapter.

26.useWhen: One measured number is the point of the sentence.
26.avoidWhen: The number lacks evidence or is not worth full-frame emphasis.

27.useWhen: A short verified quote adds evidence while footage remains useful.
27.avoidWhen: The quote merely paraphrases narration or requires several sentences.

28.useWhen: The speaker names a keyboard shortcut the viewer should reproduce.
28.avoidWhen: The keys are not spoken or already unmistakable on screen.

29.useWhen: The viewer must focus on one exact UI region without hiding it.
29.avoidWhen: The spotlight obscures the target or a zoom already solves readability.

31.useWhen: Four categories genuinely depend on two named axes.
31.avoidWhen: A simpler list or comparison communicates the point.

32.useWhen: Artur explicitly requests a share or donation breakdown backed by real values.

33.useWhen: The displayed rows are real YouTube chapters with meaningful timecodes.
33.avoidWhen: Do not use fake timestamps as decoration or substitute it for the hook agenda.

34.useWhen: A concrete safety, money, access, or data warning needs an explicit warning treatment.
34.avoidWhen: A general important thought belongs to accent N instead.

35.useWhen: A short exchange with a model is itself the evidence.
35.avoidWhen: A real chat capture is available and readable.

36.useWhen: A meaningful agent wait or reasoning state would otherwise look like dead time.
36.avoidWhen: Decorative loading or a delay too short to notice.

37.useWhen: The episode has a real sponsor and the disclosure copy is approved.

38.useWhen: Artur explicitly requests a segment topic label.
38.avoidWhen: Do not add topic labels routinely; narration and chapter markers should carry structure.

39.useWhen: Artur explicitly approves a cold-open card for this hook.
39.avoidWhen: The hook starts with useful live material or screencast evidence.

40.useWhen: A short voice-free beat needs a kinetic list and Artur approves it.
40.avoidWhen: Narrated agenda or in-body explanation; its fixed rhythm should not fight speech.

41.useWhen: A real failure or broken state is the point of the beat.

42.useWhen: A real chapter boundary uses the approved ticker transition style.
42.avoidWhen: Inside an explanation or mixed with another transition family.

43.useWhen: Telegram is mentioned and a quiet reminder can sit behind the main content.
43.avoidWhen: No spoken Telegram relevance or another CTA is already on screen.

44.useWhen: The narration explicitly invites viewers to the Telegram channel and the QR should remain alongside footage.
44.avoidWhen: No spoken CTA; never use the personal @Art_Cog account.

A.useWhen: One spoken word is the strongest beat and benefits from a large typographic hit.

B.useWhen: One short phrase contains a precise word-level emphasis.

C.useWhen: A real old and new price or tariff is stated.

E.useWhen: A genuinely strong or high-energy spoken moment earns the fire treatment.
E.avoidWhen: More than the few strongest moments; do not dilute it.

F.useWhen: A verified numeric result is the key payoff.

H.useWhen: Two short lines form a real setup/payoff or before/after thought.
H.avoidWhen: The relationship needs a table or more context.

I.useWhen: The narration explicitly replaces one term or interpretation with another.
I.avoidWhen: Ordinary correction or decorative word swapping.

J.useWhen: A short phrase needs restrained emphasis without a plate.
J.avoidWhen: A main important thought should use N or the screen is already text-heavy.

K.useWhen: A clear spoken question immediately precedes its answer.
K.avoidWhen: Rhetorical filler or questions without an immediate payoff.

L.useWhen: A short path, version, caveat, or side note adds useful context.
L.avoidWhen: The aside is the main thought or needs several sentences.

M.useWhen: A longer explanation needs a compact supporting paragraph and the source remains secondary.
M.avoidWhen: The paragraph duplicates narration or hides actionable UI.

N.useWhen: The narration reaches an important takeaway, rule, or warning; this is the primary accent treatment.
N.avoidWhen: Minor facts or decorative repetition; literal safety warnings may use 34.

O.useWhen: A real insight, realization, or useful inference is spoken.
O.avoidWhen: Generic explanation without an insight beat.

agenda-light-chips.useWhen: During the hook, the narration lists three to five things the viewer will get.
agenda-light-chips.avoidWhen: No spoken agenda, or items cannot be aligned to transcript cues.
rules: each item starts on its matching spoken cue
never use a fixed decorative stagger

process-rail-light.useWhen: During the main video, the narration enumerates steps that benefit from staying visible.
process-rail-light.avoidWhen: Hook agenda, decorative lists, or content that is already clear in the source.

agenda-dark-chips.useWhen: The source and episode require the approved dark alternate.
agenda-dark-chips.avoidWhen: Default selection; Artur prefers the light theme.
rules: same timing and geometry as light agenda
